title: Retina scan (OCT)
what: A safe picture of the retina and the optic nerve, taken with light. You look into a machine, and nothing touches your eye.
why: For worse vision, wavy or bent lines, diabetes, glaucoma, or retina disease, and to track how treatment is working.
duration: usually 5 to 15 minutes; if your pupils are widened, another 20 to 30 minutes of waiting
tell_doctor: Glaucoma or allergy to eye drops, if your pupils will be widened

prepare.title: Contact lenses
prepare.text: Contact lenses are taken out before the scan. Bring your lens case.

prepare.title: Eyes
prepare.text: Do not wear mascara that day. It can get in the way.

prepare.title: Pupils
prepare.text: Sometimes drops are used to widen your pupils. Then everything is blurry for a few hours. You cannot drive, so it is better to come with someone.

bring: Sunglasses, if your pupils will be widened
steps: If needed, drops are put in and you wait for the pupils to widen
You sit, rest your chin on a support, and press your forehead against a bar
You look at a glowing dot inside the machine
Try not to blink for a few seconds while the picture is taken
The same is done for the other eye
feel: After pupil drops: blurry close-up vision, and bright light hurts your eyes
after: Without drops, you can go back to your day right away
After drops, vision usually returns to normal in 4 to 6 hours. Do not drive until then
Images and a report are usually given the same day. An eye doctor reviews them
red_flags: Sudden loss of vision, flashes of light, or a curtain over your eye: see an eye doctor right away or call emergency services

faq.q: Is OCT harmful for the eyes?
faq.a: No. The machine uses safe light, with no radiation. The scan can be repeated as often as needed.

faq.q: Can I drive after an OCT?
faq.a: If your pupils were not widened, yes. If drops were used, no, not until your vision is clear again, usually 4 to 6 hours.
